name: @shuji-bonji/s1000d-reader-mcp

tools.name: list_data_modules
tools.description: List the CSDB objects (data modules by default; optionally publication modules, DML, DDN, IMF, UPF, ICN) in the CSDB folders with DMC parts, techName/infoName, issue, language, schema name (descript/proced/…), S1000D issue and applicability display text. A DML or DDN row also carries its code, issue date, entry/item count and a reconciliation summary against the CSDB (found / issue-mismatch / not-found / not-checked; for a DML also how many DMs and PMs it does not list). Filter by modelIdentCode, systemCode, infoCode, schemaName or title text. Paged with offset/limit.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

schemaName.description: descript / proced / process / fault / pm / brex / …

text.description: Case-insensitive text to find in techName or infoName.

tools.name: read_data_module
tools.description: Read one data module as structure, not XML: identification and status (DMC, issue, language, title, BREX ref, QA, DM-level applicability), the body as a tree of blocks (sections, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures with ICN, warnings/cautions/notes, numbered steps, requirements; processes and fault isolation too), the references it makes, ALWAYS a "verification" status (XSD by default) and ALWAYS "securityClassification" (the data module's value and the values carried by elements in the body, uninterpreted) at the top of the response. section "outline" returns a summary (headings, step numbers, first sentence, size of each subtree) for deciding what to read. Applicability of each block is evaluated for the given product (applicable / notApplicable / undetermined); without a product, only display texts are returned — assert expressions are never returned.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

dmc.description: DMC of the data module to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A"; "DMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

product.description: The product to evaluate applicability for. attributes: ACT productAttribute id → value (e.g. {"model": "Brook trekker", "version": "Mk9"}); conditions: CCT cond id → value. Omit to get "undetermined" with display texts only. Use describe_applicability to learn the available ids and values.

section.description: Which part to return (default all). "outline" returns only headings, step numbers, the first sentence and the size (nodes / chars / admonitions) of each subtree — call it first on a large data module to decide what to read.

outlineDepth.description: With section "outline": how many levels of headings / steps to return (default: all levels).

verify.description: How much to verify before reading: "schema" (default) runs XSD validation only; "full" also checks BREX along the brexDmRef chain and resolves references; "none" skips verification (reported as not-run).

omitNotApplicable.description: Drop blocks that are notApplicable for the given product (default false: keep them, marked). The number dropped is reported.

tools.name: read_publication_module
tools.description: Read a publication module (PMC) as a table of contents: the pmEntry tree with titles, and for each dmRef/pmRef the resolved target (file, techName/infoName, issue) from the CSDB. Also returns the PM identification and a verification status.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

pmc.description: PMC to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-B6865-EPWG1-00"; "PMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

verify.description: How much to verify before reading: "schema" (default) runs XSD validation only; "full" also checks BREX along the brexDmRef chain and resolves references; "none" skips verification (reported as not-run).

tools.name: resolve_reference
tools.description: Resolve one reference to a CSDB object: a DMC, a PMC, or an ICN (file name or entity name). Returns the file path(s), issue(s) and title. For an ICN, pass "fromPath" of the data module whose DOCTYPE declares the entity to get the declared file and notation.

icn.description: ICN (entity name or file name) to resolve.

fromPath.description: Data module whose DOCTYPE declares the ICN entity (optional).

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

tools.name: describe_applicability
tools.description: Describe the applicability vocabulary of a data module so a product can be chosen: the ACT product attributes (ids, names, enumerations/patterns, which one identifies the product), the CCT condition types and conditions, the PCT products (ready-made product values), the applic statements in the data module (ids and display texts), and which attributes used by the statements have no value in the PCT. Nothing is evaluated here; pass the chosen values as "product" to read_data_module.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

dmc.description: DMC of the data module to read from the CSDB (e.g. "S1000DBIKE-AAA-D00-00-00-00AA-041A-A"; "DMC-" prefix optional). Alternative to path/xml.

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

tools.name: read_icn_metadata
tools.description: Read an ICN metadata file (IMF, icnmetadata.xsd): ICN, issue, title, keywords, security, source/originator and other status items as a flat list, plus the related ICN files found in the CSDB.

xml.description: The document as an XML string (alternative to path; max 5 MB).

icn.description: ICN whose IMF to read from the CSDB (e.g. "C0419-S1000D0360-001-01" or "ICN-C0419-…").

csdbDirs.description: CSDB folders to search for data modules by DMC, referenced objects, ACT/CCT/PCT and BREX (default: S1000D_CSDB_DIR / the config file). When given, these folders replace S1000D_CSDB_DIR and the csdbDirs of the config file (they are not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and reported in _notes.

instructions:
This server READS S1000D data modules and publication modules as structure (sections, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures with ICN, warnings/cautions/notes, numbered steps, requirements, process flows, fault isolation questions, PM tables of contents) and EVALUATES applicability for a product. Every response carries "verification" (VerificationStatus): schema (valid / invalid / schema-not-found / not-run), brex and references ("not-run" unless verify="full"), and every read_data_module / read_publication_module response starts with "securityClassification" (the document's value and the values carried by elements in the body, as written — decide how to handle the content before quoting it; the server does not interpret the values).

It does NOT do the following:
- It does not return applicability expressions (assert/evaluate). The server evaluates them for the "product" you pass and returns applicable / notApplicable / undetermined with the human-readable displayText. "undetermined" means the product lacks a needed value (see reason) or no product was given — it is not "does not apply". Call describe_applicability to learn the attribute ids and values (ACT/CCT/PCT) and the values the PCT leaves unassigned.
- It does not decide S1000D conformance and does not list BREX or XSD errors in detail; use s1000d-verify-mcp for that and s1000d-brex-mcp to explain BREX rules.
- It does not summarize or translate. It keeps headings, step numbers, admonition levels and references ([→ DMC title] inline and in refs) so you can.
- It does not ship any S1000D specification, XSD or sample. XSD validation needs S1000D_SPEC_DIR (the extracted S1000D distribution) or {"specDir": "/absolute/path"} in ~/.config/s1000d-stack/config.json (for hosts that do not pass environment variables to plugins); the CSDB is found via S1000D_CSDB_DIR, "csdbDirs" in that config file, or the "csdbDirs" argument. When the "csdbDirs" argument is given, it replaces the other two (it is not added to them); folders that do not exist are skipped and listed in _notes.

Reading results: if verification.schema is schema-not-found or invalid, the structure may be misread — say so. Elements the reader does not know are kept as kind "unknown" with their text and counted in content.unknownElements. Data module kinds other than descript / proced / process / fault / pm return structured: false with identAndStatus only. References to the specification (modelIdentCode "S1000D") are not listed as unresolved.

Costly options: read_data_module with verify="full" runs BREX checks (about 0.1 s per data module). list_data_modules reads every file for titles; narrow with filter.

Budget: on a large data module call read_data_module with section "outline" first. It returns headings, step numbers, the first sentence of each and the size of each subtree (nodes / chars / warnings), without the body or the references; content.size says how big the full body is. Then read section "content" (optionally with maxNodes) once you know what you need.

An input the server cannot use comes back as {"error": {"code": "...", "path": "/path", "detail": "..."}} (not as a tool failure), in the same shape as s1000d-writer-mcp. code is "file-not-found" (the file at that argument does not exist), "no-csdb" (no CSDB folder exists; pass "csdbDirs"), "not-found" (the DMC, PMC or ICN is not in the CSDB) or "input-error" (the argument is malformed or missing). path names the argument to fix. Fix it and call again.
